name: PyField
description: D1 field-grain population on the Python (aws/pipeline) substrates. The estate's dependency graph carries field-grain value flow -- which field feeds which field, by what method -- on the PORTAL substrate ONLY: FLOWS_TO (961) and PROP_PASSES (1382) are 100% layer=portal, and on the substrates where every gold script lives, field grain does not exist in the graph at all. This project populates it so comp-pipescript can emit a per-script field IO list and comp-dataflow can walk it BACKWARD -- the migration question, 'if I change this field, what breaks downstream'. Born as the residue of the SCRIPT_IO S-layer, which was DISSOLVED (zero new vocabulary) after measurement showed every capability it proposed was already live on 961 edges.

arch_rulings: MECHANISM: flow-local inference (binding-side) WITH declare-the-limit as MANDATORY coverage policy -- NOT a type-inference dependency. Build Ladder rung 5 run: mypy/pyright/pytype/jedi all ABSENT, so 'buy inference' is add-a-dependency, not use-what-we-have. 'Declare the limit' is not a third option -- 'provably a DataFrame' IS the binding-side mechanism, so choosing it as the cheap option buys the build unscoped.

TOOL FIT (Andrew asked which it fits with better): BOTH, at the two ends of one rail. comp-pipescript = EXTRACTION per script (already has _extract_column_gaps at extract_pipeline.py:981); comp-dataflow = TRAVERSAL across scripts. The rule bank already ruled it at NFRA_ONTOLOGY_RULE_BANK.yaml:324 -- 'provenance/canonical-origin = D1 grain + D2 path walked BACKWARD (comp-dataflow ...) becomes a QUERY over D1+D2, not a bespoke tool'. The migration question is a backward walk.

THREE MECHANISMS, build all three: binding-side (27.6%), usage-side (23.1%, +4 to +14 pts NET-NEW, only 34.6% overlap -- largely independent), and exclusion-side which is ALREADY RUNNING in comp-pipescript. Union of the first two = 41.1%.

THE EXCLUSION SET MUST BE DERIVED, NOT LIFTED. _DF_METHODS is hand-drawn, incident-driven (2026-04-14), 71 names against a real universe of 240 (dir(DataFrame) u dir(Series), pandas 2.3.3) -- it MISSES 170 (70.8%), carries one member that is not a DataFrame attribute at all (concat), and is not version-pinned. Derive it at runtime from the installed pandas API: one line, self-maintaining, closes 170 gaps by construction.
